name.purpose: The line's name in the hero, in the 5x7 pixel face from tools/logo.py; 42px, 56px from 640px, multiples of 7 so font pixels stay whole.

tagline.purpose: The line's one line under the name; 18px, 20px from 640px. The only Inter text above body size.

body.purpose: All reading text, Paper Ink or Soft Ink, prose capped at 65ch.

title.purpose: Every heading: weight 500 at body size.

control.purpose: coss button and input text; 16px below 640px, 14px above.

mono.purpose: File names, round trip, short fingerprints, list markers.

code.purpose: A computer's full code, three lines of grouped quads, selectable as a whole.

shadows.name: window-lift
shadows.purpose: Only on a copy of an app's window standing in the night field.

shadows.name: prompt-edge
shadows.purpose: The prompt card over its 55% black dim; containers on the ground.

shadows.name: paper-button
shadows.purpose: coss primary button at rest; removed on press and when disabled.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A pressed button dips; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: appear
motion.purpose: A prompt arriving; fade only under reduced motion.

motion.name: field-develop
motion.value: 1400ms, exponential ease-out (1 - 2^(-10k)), left-to-right front with Bayer-order landing
motion.purpose: The night field develops once; drawn at once under reduced motion.

motion.name: link-forming
motion.purpose: The link meter while a connection forms.

motion.name: link-settle
motion.purpose: A live link filling in to its quality.

motion.name: link-lost
motion.purpose: Sparse violet while the link is lost.

motion.name: stats-fade
motion.purpose: The route and round trip appearing under the link.

narrative.overview:
Each line's README banner, the night field of Bayer-dithered dusk dots with the line's 32x32 mark in the glow and its name in the 5x7 pixel face, is the top of the page, live. The name, the line, the download and the line's running piece sit inside that field as working parts. Below it the night dithers out onto luannzin.com's neutral ground, and the rest of the page is his site's interface: one near-black ground, paper ink in three tiers, white-alpha hairlines, Inter at one size.

The page is dark only, like the apps. Colour lives in the art (the field, the marks, the link between windows) and, inside a copy of an app's own window, in that app's own meanings. The chrome of the page never takes a hue. Density is low: a narrow column of words on the left of the field, sections on the ground set with their title beside them, generous space between them.

A line brings its words, its mark and its live piece; the page around them is shared (`Line` and `Part`). New lines inherit the template rather than designing their own.
keyCharacteristics: A night field (#110d24) of 2px dots on a 3px grid, dithered toward a dusk glow around the line's mark; calm under the words.
The night ends in a Bayer dither onto the ground, never on a straight edge.
Inter at one size, hierarchy by weight 500 and ink tier; Geist Mono for codes, file names and measurements.
Marks and pixel type at whole-pixel multiples only.
Every motion has a reduced-motion state that is complete, not missing.

rules.name: The Colour Is the Art's Rule
rules.body: The page's own chrome (text, links, buttons, rules, selection, focus) stays on the neutral axis. A hue appears only as dithered dots, or as an app's own meaning inside a copy of its window.

rules.name: The Every Grey Is a Dither Rule
rules.body: In the art, a lighter or darker passage is made by dot density in Bayer order, never by a fill, gradient, blur or opacity. The night itself ends the same way.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Inside a window copy, red means someone is in and green means you have control. Neither is used for anything else, on the window or off it.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Inter is 16px for everything you read. A heading gets weight 500 and full ink, never a larger size; the tagline is the single exception.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Rule
rules.body: Pixel type and pixel marks scale only by whole multiples: the name in multiples of 7px, the 32x32 mark at 1x, 3x and 8x, always with `image-rendering: pixelated` and crisp edges.

rules.name: The Inset Edge Rule
rules.body: Containers on the ground are edged by a 1px inset ring or a hairline rule. An outer shadow belongs only to an app window shown floating in the field.

dos: **Do** build a new line from `Line` and `Part`, bringing only its words, its 32x32 mark and its live piece.
**Do** draw every passage of the art in 2px dots on the 3px grid, in the 4x4 Bayer order, from the night and the four dusk colours only.
**Do** end the night in a dither onto the ground.
**Do** set the line's name in the pixel face at a multiple of 7px, with the text name available to screen readers.
**Do** keep one paper-ink button per group, and put the detected system's file first, with its exact file name and what the system says the first time.
**Do** give every motion a reduced-motion state that still shows the result: field drawn at once, link strips still, prompts fading without scale.
**Do** keep every string in English and Brazilian Portuguese.
donts: **Don't** give the page's chrome a hue: no accent links, buttons, focus rings or selection colours.
**Don't** use the dusk as a fill, gradient or blur, or anywhere it isn't dots.
**Don't** use a window copy's red or green outside that window, or for anything but its meaning.
**Don't** raise an Inter heading above 16px; use weight 500 and full ink.
**Don't** scale a mark or the pixel name by fractional amounts or smooth it.
**Don't** add a light theme; the lines are dark, like the apps.
**Don't** show the app through a GIF, video or mock; a line's live piece runs for real.
